WHAT IT COVERS

When flood cleanup is the right service

Flood Cleanup can be relevant after plumbing failures, appliance leaks, roof leaks, storms, flooding or other events that leave building materials wet. The correct scope depends on the water source, contamination category, affected materials and how long the area has been wet.

A professional assessment should identify visible and hidden moisture, document affected areas and establish a practical sequence for removal, drying, cleaning and repair.

What to have ready when you call

  • Property address and ZIP
  • Where the water started
  • Whether the source is still active
  • Rooms/materials affected
  • Whether sewage or other contamination is involved
PROCESS

A measured restoration response

Inspect the source and affected areas

Identify where water entered, how it traveled and whether materials outside the visible area are damp.

Remove standing or trapped water

Extraction and removal methods are selected according to depth, access, material type and contamination.

Dry and monitor

Air movement and dehumidification are paired with moisture readings so drying is based on evidence rather than guesswork.

Clean, repair or refer for reconstruction

Once the structure is appropriately dry, damaged finishes may be cleaned, treated, repaired or replaced according to the actual scope.

FAQ

Questions people ask before calling

How do I know if I need flood cleanup?

The service is generally relevant when the property condition matches its scope. A professional assessment can determine whether flood cleanup or a related service is appropriate.

Is the service available for homes and businesses?

Many restoration providers serve both residential and commercial properties, but availability and scope should be confirmed with the provider you are connected with.

Will the provider handle insurance?

Some providers assist with documentation or insurance processes; this varies by provider and policy. Ask the provider exactly what they handle before work begins.

What if the water is contaminated?

Avoid contact and keep people and pets away. Sewage and other contaminated water require different safety procedures than clean-water incidents.
